claims.statement: The fixed radix is B=1000=2^3*5^3 and the canonical coefficient set is {0,...,999}.
claims.proof_reference: Part I; postulates K3-A1 and K3-A2

claims.statement: A finite coefficient profile a=(a_0,...,a_m), indexed from least significant to most significant, has value sum_i a_i*1000^i.
Every n in N_0 has exactly one finite canonical base-1000 coefficient profile.

scope.domain: n in N_0
assumptions: B=1000 is fixed
Every coefficient is the Euclidean remainder in 0..999
scope.boundary: Finite canonical expansions only; signed values are handled by the separate sign extension.

claims.statement: The symbol k is a lexical group separator; a terminal k denotes exactly one implicit low-order zero group.
Strict canonical words, K3-PAD imports and typed K3-RAW operands are distinct input types.
Euclidean carry/borrow normalization preserves the polynomial value and yields a canonical coefficient profile under the stated finite-vector assumptions.
claims.proof_reference: §§2.1–2.8, local balance and telescoping global invariant

scope.domain: Finite integer coefficient vectors
assumptions: Each local step uses Euclidean quotient and remainder
The input vector is finite
scope.boundary: The binary carry bound is not asserted for arbitrary signed raw coefficients.

claims.statement: For every r>=1, Z/1000^r Z is isomorphic to Z/2^(3r) Z x Z/5^(3r) Z.

scope.domain: r in integers with r>=1
assumptions: The moduli 2^(3r) and 5^(3r) are coprime
scope.boundary: This is a classical CRT specialization, not a claim that Z/1000^r Z is a field.

claims.statement: The inverse-limit completion for the 1000-adic ideal filtration is Z_2 x Z_5 as a topological ring.

scope.domain: Inverse system Z/1000^r Z for r>=1
assumptions: The transition maps are the canonical reduction maps
The inverse-limit topology is used
scope.boundary: The completion is a topological ring; it is not a field.

claims.statement: Canonicalization preserves numeric evaluation; structural equality and expression-tree equality remain separately typed.

scope.domain: The separately typed K3 canonical, PAD and RAW input profiles
assumptions: Canonicalization is defined only for accepted PAD/RAW inputs
The value map is the polynomial evaluation over B=1000
scope.boundary: Structural or AST equality is not implied by numerical equality.

claims.statement: The finite Hankel moment determinant admits the stated weighted squared-Vandermonde expansion for a finite nonnegative coefficient profile.

scope.domain: Finite nonnegative profiles a=(a_0,...,a_m) and finite moment order q
assumptions: Moment and Hankel matrices use the definitions in §3
scope.boundary: The determinant expansion is a Cauchy-Binet/Vandermonde specialization, not a general priority claim.

claims.statement: The position-and-length polynomial of maximal zero runs reconstructs the zero mask of the finite profile.

scope.domain: Finite profiles with zero positions in {0,...,m}
assumptions: The zero-run list contains all maximal zero intervals exactly once
scope.boundary: The zero mask does not recover nonzero coefficient magnitudes.

claims.statement: The finite lag spectrum satisfies the stated zero-lag, reciprocity and total-sum identities for aligned finite profiles.

scope.domain: Two finite aligned profiles with the same declared finite depth
assumptions: Out-of-range coordinates are handled according to the chapter's zero-extension convention
scope.boundary: The lag spectrum does not in general determine the complete pair of profiles.

claims.statement: For addition of two nonnegative canonical profiles, carry values are binary and the weighted local balance telescopes to the global sum identity.

scope.domain: Two finite nonnegative canonical K3 profiles
assumptions: Each input coefficient belongs to 0..999
The initial carry is zero
scope.boundary: Binary carry is not claimed for arbitrary raw signed coefficient vectors or an arbitrary number of addends.

claims.statement: The K3-M appendix contains five parameterized families of 937 records each, for 4685 unique identifiers; records instantiate five master schemes and are not 4685 independent discoveries.
claims.proof_reference: §§0, 3–5; five master schemas and catalogue tables

claims.statement: The 1000-divisibility depth is the minimum of the quantized 2-adic and 5-adic depths.

scope.domain: n in Z\{0} and r in N_0
assumptions: v_2 and v_5 are the ordinary prime-adic valuations
scope.boundary: The base-1000 divisibility depth is a minimum of two quantized valuations, not an additive prime valuation.

claims.statement: The defect of additivity of 1000-divisibility depth under products is given by the exact two-channel compensation term stated in the chapter.

scope.domain: Nonzero integers x,y
assumptions: The two prime valuations are finite on nonzero integers
The complementarity term is defined from the remainders modulo 3
scope.boundary: Do not infer additivity of the 1000-divisibility depth.

claims.statement: The residue-tree branching coordinates at every level form the stated bijection between the 8-channel and 125-channel residue coordinates.

scope.domain: Finite level r>=1 of the residue tree
assumptions: The coordinate maps are those specified in §5
scope.boundary: The result is an explicit CRT coordinate description, not a new arithmetic base.

claims.statement: The 1000-adic ultrametric equals the maximum of the two channel ultrametrics under the chapter's definitions.

scope.domain: Distinct integers x,y with the channel metrics defined in §6
assumptions: Both channel metrics are defined from the 2- and 5-adic valuations
The product metric is their maximum
scope.boundary: No claim is made that either channel alone induces the K3 metric.

claims.statement: For independent uniform input groups and a fixed incoming carry, the conditional joint distribution of output group and next carry is the one stated in the chapter.

scope.domain: A,D independent and uniform on D_B; fixed c in {0,1}
assumptions: B is an integer >=2
R=(A+D+c) mod B
C'=floor((A+D+c)/B)
scope.boundary: The law is conditional on a fixed incoming carry and does not imply independence of R and C'.

claims.statement: Under independent uniform input groups and fixed incoming carry, Corr(R,C'|c)=-1/sqrt(3), for every integer base B>=2.

scope.domain: A,D independent and uniform on D_B; fixed c in {0,1}
assumptions: B is an integer >=2
R and C' are as defined in §7
The correlation is conditional on c
scope.boundary: The coefficient -1/sqrt(3) is not asserted for nonuniform or dependent inputs.

claims.statement: The associated graded ring of the 1000-adic ideal filtration on Z is isomorphic to (Z/1000Z)[T].

scope.domain: The ring Z with ideal filtration I^r=(1000^r)
assumptions: The associated graded ring uses I^r/I^(r+1)
The grading is by r>=0
scope.boundary: The graded ring is a classical construction for this filtration, not a field.

claims.statement: For bounded linear operators on a common space, swapping adjacent factors in a product changes the product by the surrounding factors times the commutator.

scope.domain: Finite products of bounded linear operators on one common normed space
assumptions: All factors are bounded and composable
The commutator is [A,B]=AB-BA
scope.boundary: The formula does not apply to nonlinear operators without a separate definition and proof.

claims.statement: Under the explicitly stated nearest-frame rounding model, cumulative duration error is bounded by the sum of the half-target-frame periods.

scope.domain: A finite sequence of nearest-frame resampling stages with positive target rates f_j
assumptions: Each stage contributes at most half a target frame of rounding error
Durations are compared in the same unit
scope.boundary: The theorem does not prove spectral equivalence, absence of aliasing or amplitude preservation.

claims.statement: A transition that only removes capabilities or budget cannot increase the represented feasible-state set under the stated subset order.

scope.domain: A transition system ordered by inclusion of feasible-state sets
assumptions: Each transition only removes capabilities or budget
The feasibility predicate is monotone with respect to the stated order
scope.boundary: This abstract result does not prove that a particular software system enforces its declared constraints.

claims.statement: A distributional law for the two-channel complementarity index may hold under an explicitly chosen random model.
A spectral classification of operator chains may be available for selected operator classes.
A dimensionally complete K3-X typing discipline may be developed for a larger class of homogeneous quantities.
Sharper cumulative error bounds may be proved for selected multistage resampling models.
A joint proof-evidence graph may be specified with machine-checkable provenance rules.
The Pytyliki-to-K3 document is an application-level mathematical reconstruction with explicit implementation and evidence boundaries, not a theorem about full runtime correctness.
The OPlague-to-K3 materials define an application mathematical model and provenance boundaries; they do not extend the base K3 axioms.
claims.proof_reference: Part XI and Part XII; K3 mapping and proof obligations

claims.statement: The implication nu_1000(n)=0 => n is a unit modulo 1000^r is false.
claims.witness: For n=8 and r=1, nu_1000(8)=0 but gcd(8,1000)=8, so [8] is not a unit.

scope.domain: Integers n and r>=1
assumptions: The modulus is 1000^r
nu_1000 is divisibility depth by powers of 1000
scope.boundary: The correct unit criterion is gcd(n,1000)=1.

claims.statement: The function nu_1000 is additive on multiplication for all nonzero integer pairs.

scope.domain: Nonzero integer pairs
assumptions: nu_1000(n) is the greatest r such that 1000^r divides n
scope.boundary: The witness refutes additivity, not every divisibility inequality.

claims.statement: The number of separators k uniquely determines the numeric value of a K3 word.
claims.witness: 50k0k and 5k0k each have two separators but evaluate to 50000000 and 5000000.

scope.domain: Finite canonical nonnegative K3 words
assumptions: Both words use radix 1000 and canonical syntax
scope.boundary: Separator count records depth, not the full coefficient profile.

claims.statement: The quotient ring Z/1000Z is a field.
claims.witness: [8] and [125] are nonzero modulo 1000 but their product is [1000]=[0].

scope.domain: The quotient ring Z/1000Z
assumptions: Residue classes are taken modulo 1000
scope.boundary: A field has no nonzero zero divisors.

claims.statement: Equal numeric evaluations imply identity of ordered expression trees.
claims.witness: Add(50k,K3-RAW(5k0)) and Add(K3-RAW(5k0),50k) are distinct ordered trees but both evaluate to 55000.

scope.domain: Ordered binary addition expressions over typed K3 operands
assumptions: Both operands are evaluated as integers
Addition is ordinary integer addition
scope.boundary: Numeric equality does not erase AST order or operation provenance.

claims.statement: K3-GCS-1 is the typed tuple of a dependency graph, an algebraic category, a sign-interpretation category, graph-to-category and sign mappings, and interpretation rules.
A K3-GCS dependency graph is a typed directed multigraph whose vertices and edges carry declared types, labels, contextual guards, and optional weights.
A semiotic passport is the typed triple of representamen, represented object, and interpretant rule, with an optional interpretation context.
The four-valued evidence domain consists of true, false, unknown, and conflict states represented by positive and negative evidence pairs.

For selected classes of K3 dependency graphs, quotienting by equivalences that preserve semantic passports and categorical invariants may yield a smaller model without losing a specified set of derivations.
claims.proof_reference: §15.1, Hypothesis GCS-1; proof obligation is open

scope.domain: Selected finite or suitably bounded typed K3 dependency graphs
assumptions: The quotient relation is explicitly defined
Semantic passports and selected categorical invariants are preserved
scope.boundary: No general derivation-preservation theorem is claimed for arbitrary graph quotients.

claims.statement: For a defined class of predicate systems over finite metadata domains, the cascade refinement operator may be monotone and may reach a least or greatest fixed point.
claims.proof_reference: §15.1, Hypothesis GCS-2; proof obligation is open

scope.domain: Specified finite partially ordered metadata states and predicate operators
assumptions: A partial order is defined
Every refinement operator is proved monotone
The update schedule satisfies the stated fairness condition
scope.boundary: Termination is not claimed for arbitrary non-monotone or infinite-state cascades.

claims.statement: For some covers of K3 metadata graphs, compatible local passports may glue uniquely into a global structure satisfying the sheaf conditions.
claims.proof_reference: §15.1, Hypothesis GCS-3; proof obligation is open

scope.domain: A specified base space, cover, presheaf of metadata, and restriction maps
assumptions: Local sections are defined
Compatibility on overlaps is defined
The relevant sheaf axioms are checked
scope.boundary: Pairwise local compatibility alone does not establish a unique global section.

claims.statement: Some metadata morphisms may induce maps between Schwarz planes that preserve selected dimension or tensor invariants.
claims.proof_reference: §15.1, Hypothesis GCS-4; proof obligation is open

scope.domain: A specified family of metadata morphisms and the associated Schwarz-plane configurations
assumptions: The metadata-to-coordinate maps are fixed
The class of admissible morphisms is specified
The dimension or tensor invariant is defined on both sides
scope.boundary: No invariant-preservation claim is made for arbitrary morphisms or all Schwarz-plane configurations.

claims.statement: A numbering collapse occurs when an equivalence relation on a common semantic carrier identifies every numbered value with one distinguished void state; the induced factor numbering is the quotient projection composed with the original numbering.

scope.domain: A numbering nu:I->U and an equivalence relation on U
assumptions: The distinguished void state belongs to the same carrier U
Every numbered value is equivalent to the distinguished state
scope.boundary: The definition concerns loss of distinguishability in a quotient and does not delete the index set or the original numbers.

claims.statement: If every value of a numbering is equivalent to one distinguished void state, its induced quotient numbering is constant and is non-injective whenever the index set has at least two elements.

scope.domain: A numbering nu:I->U with |I|>=2
assumptions: An equivalence relation is defined on U
Every nu(i) is equivalent to the distinguished void state
scope.boundary: No claim is made that the original numbering or its index domain ceases to exist.

claims.statement: The negative-axis control model uses K(y)=K0-lambda*y on y<=0 with lambda>0, so decreasing y increases the selected control measure.

scope.domain: Real control parameter y<=0
assumptions: K0 is real
lambda is strictly positive
scope.boundary: The monotonicity follows from the chosen function and is not implied by y<0 alone.

claims.statement: The secondary inventory of descriptions is the tuple of typed description operators applied to a primary description of an object.

scope.domain: An object O with primary description delta(O) and operators P_i
assumptions: Each P_i has a declared input and output type
The operators are defined on delta(O)
scope.boundary: The resulting tuple describes descriptions and is not identified with the source object.

claims.statement: Semantic load after n steps is D_n=sum_{i=1}^n w_i*h_i with nonnegative contributions h_i and positive weights w_i.

scope.domain: Finite sequences of real contributions and weights
assumptions: w_i>0
The units and interpretation of h_i and w_i are declared for each application
scope.boundary: The decimal example in the source proposal does not by itself define a universal sequence or a semantic metric.

claims.statement: For some classes of description systems beyond a critical semantic load, increasing description complexity may decrease the operational recoverability of the described object.

scope.domain: A declared class of description systems with a measurable recoverability function R(P,D)
assumptions: Recoverability is operationally defined on [0,1]
A critical load threshold is specified
The comparison holds the object class and measurement protocol fixed
scope.boundary: The claim is not universal; lossless encodings can increase description length without reducing recoverability.

claims.statement: The paradigmatic-erosion feedback model is the discrete recurrence for description complexity, semantic load, and recoverability given in equation (PE-5).

scope.domain: Discrete state variables p_n,e_n,r_n and positive parameters alpha,beta,gamma
assumptions: p_n>=0, e_n>=0 and r_n in [0,1]
alpha,beta,gamma are strictly positive
scope.boundary: The recurrence is a chosen model and is not asserted to represent every description process.

claims.statement: For recurrence (PE-5) with positive parameters, positive initial load, and positive initial recoverability, semantic load and description complexity diverge while recoverability converges to zero.

scope.domain: The discrete recurrence (PE-5)
assumptions: alpha>0, beta>0, gamma>0
scope.boundary: The result proves the recurrence's behavior only; it is not a universal theorem about formal systems.

claims.statement: A K3-NS record is a typed many-sorted tuple separating the source object, encoding profile, canonical K3 vector and value, structural profile, relation graph, context, interpretation set, and provenance; every map between components is explicitly typed.
claims.proof_reference: §1.2, typed numerative record and canonical contract
claims.verification_note: The tuple is a compatible semantic overlay; it does not redefine the K3 value function or the lexical separator.

claims.statement: K3-NS keeps source-object equality, code equality, numeric-value equality, structural relations, graph relations, and contextual interpretation as distinct typed relations unless an explicit mapping and equivalence criterion is supplied.
claims.proof_reference: §2, equality layers, collisions, and typed relations
claims.verification_note: A collision in one encoding profile does not imply semantic equivalence, causality, prediction, or a cryptographic property.
